newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt libel trial opens, adjourned for a week.
newsitem.headline: Egypt libel trial opens, adjourned for a week.

text.p: Six men accused of libelling the two businessmen sons of Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak went on trial on Sunday but the judge adjourned the case for a week at the defence's request.
The defence sought the postponement so that they could have more time to prepare their statement.
The defendants are charged with publishing corruption allegations against Alaa and Gamal Mubarak which appeared in Asharq al-Awsat, a London-based newspaper close to the Saudi Arabian government.

The Mubaraks complained to the prosecutor last month about the allegations published in an advertisement for an issue of the newspaper's sister magazine, al-Jadida. The article was withdrawn before distribution.
Defence lawyer Ibrahim Saleh told reporters he expected Mubarak's sons to withdraw the case after the defendants published an apology in Asharq al-Awsat.

The defendants include Hisham and Mohammed Hafez, the Saudi publishers of Asharq al-Awsat, and the daily's editor-in-chief, Othman al-Omaer. An Egyptian journalist and two former editors of al-Jadida are also being prosecuted.
